title: Kikwiflow draft process specification
description: Structural companion to model-kikwi-process' draft mode (Step 0) — for a business/specification sketch that is NOT yet meant to deploy or document existing code, built incrementally with a non-technical stakeholder who doesn't have (and shouldn't be forced to invent) answers to deploy-time technical questions yet. Same 15 node types and the same top-level/edge shape as kikwi-deploy.schema.json, but every node-type-specific technical field (executor, providerType/providerBean/providerVariable, attachedToRef, calledElement, schedulePolicy, ...) is optional here, and none of the cross-field semantic rules (at most one isDefault edge, GROUP+STATIC forbidden, elementVariable needs collectionVariable) are enforced — a real sketch is allowed to be incomplete or briefly inconsistent mid-conversation. This schema still requires a name/type per node and catches actual typos (an unknown field name, a node type outside the real 15, a dangling edge shape) — the two things a rough sketch has no excuse to get wrong. A file that only validates against this schema is NOT deploy-ready: run it back through model-kikwi-process in deploy mode (checked against kikwi-deploy.schema.json) once the technical decisions this schema deliberately doesn't ask for are actually known.

sequenceFlow.description: id/targetNodeId are still required — an edge that doesn't say where it goes isn't a sketch, it's a typo. Everything gateway-specific (isDefault, handlesNull, expectedAnswer) stays optional and unconstrained: a draft is allowed to leave routing rules undecided, or briefly inconsistent (e.g. two isDefault edges while still figuring out the branches), without that blocking the sketch.

baseNodeFields.description: id/name/type are still required — a node needs a name even in a sketch (the name usually *is* the content at this stage); everything below is the same shape as the deploy schema, just without any of it being mandatory.

flowNodeUnion.description: A single shared node schema, deliberately NOT branched per node type the way kikwi-deploy.schema.json's flowNodeUnion is: the whole point of draft mode is that a task, a gateway, and a boundary event all reduce to 'id + name + type + maybe a technical field nobody's decided yet' — there's no per-type required set left to differentiate. Every technical field any of the 15 types can carry is listed below as optional and loosely typed; see skills/model-kikwi-process/reference/node-types.md for the real per-type catalog (which fields actually apply to which type, and what's required) once it's time to harden this into a deploy-grade file.

type.description: Still a closed list, even in a sketch — an invented 16th type isn't a valid draft of a Kikwiflow process, it's a different modeling language.
